_about: Name data for Ardan (c7), reworked for owner rule 11 and D-013 (one common English language, many cultures). 'common' is one large pool of plain English-language names used by most realms (1,500+ male, 1,500+ female, 4,000+ family names, 600+ places, plus trades, epithets and bynames) with patterns that multiply them. 'pools' holds the separate sounds kept only for the non-human races (elves, dwarves, orcs, giants) and three far human peoples (steppe, desert, south); each has 300+ given names per sex and 500+ family names. 'cultures' lists the 24 culture ids (CUL-01 to CUL-24) with 'uses' ('common' or a pool id), an optional small 'accent' (a few dozen English-language names that give a common-pool realm a slight local colour; draw a few from it in front of the common list) and a short 'customs' note (dress, faith, ways). Patterns: tokens <given> <surname> <father> <mother> <place> <trade> <epithet> <byname>; 'weight' picks the form (common only); a 'formFemale' replaces 'form' for women. 'uniqueFullNames' is the sum over forms and both sexes of the product of the list sizes the form uses (father = male list, mother = female list; culture counts include its accent names). Nothing is wired in yet.

common.flavour: Plain everyday English-language names used by most realms (common English and familiar European names as used in English)

patterns.rule: Plain '<given> <surname>' most often; 'of <place>', 'the <trade>' and '<byname>' for the poor, the settled or the travelling; 'son/daughter of <father>' for formal and legal use; 'the <epithet>' for a known deed or look. Surnames inherit; bynames do not. Culture accents (see cultures) add a few local names to the draw.

steppe.flavour: Turkic/Mongol-like steppe riders (far people: own sound)

patterns.rule: Mostly '<given> <surname>'; the byname forms mark trade, place or looks; father forms for formal use.

desert.flavour: Arabic/Moorish-like gardens, ports and desert nomads (far people: own sound)

patterns.rule: A man is 'ibn <father>', a woman 'bint <father>'. Trades and epithets take 'al-'. Tribes: 'Banu <tribe>'; 'abu/umm' names a parent after the eldest child.

south.flavour: South Indian / Bengali-like spice coast and monsoon plains (far people: own sound)

patterns.rule: Mostly '<given> <surname>'; the byname forms mark trade, place or looks; father forms for formal use.

forms.exampleMale: Tobias son of Daggud the Stonebeard
forms.exampleFemale: Oda daughter of Thurgrim the Tunneller

patterns.rule: Dwarves take a craft byname by their forties; father-son forms are the common case.

orc-horde.flavour: Gruff short harsh orc clan names (the Horde)

patterns.rule: Orcs name the clan first: 'Clan <name>' bynames, short given names.

orc-tusk.flavour: Harsh eastern-steppe orc names, open endings (the Tusk clans)

patterns.rule: As the Horde, but open-ending names (-gu, -gra, -ma).
Saga forms: father-son and epithet. Epithets shown in English.

CUL-01.name: Solenfolk
CUL-01.flavour: French/Italian-like (Latin heirs of an old empire)
CUL-01.customs: dress: silk and brocade, tall hats; faith: the old imperial church, saints' days; ways: courtly manners, wine, law and letters

CUL-02.name: Northfolk
CUL-02.customs: dress: wool, furs, cloaks pinned with brooches; faith: hearth rites mixed with the church; ways: farmers and knights, long feasts, oath-bound lords

CUL-03.name: Wind Riders
CUL-03.customs: dress: felt caps, leather coats, horsehair tassels; faith: sky and spirit worship, shamans; ways: horse herds, felt tents, raiding, guest-right

CUL-04.name: Qadiri
CUL-04.customs: dress: flowing robes, turbans; faith: the one-god law, scholars of the mosque; ways: gardens, ports, poetry, bargaining

CUL-05.name: Sandfolk
CUL-05.customs: dress: veils against sand; faith: desert law and tribal elders; ways: tent clans, camel caravans, feuds, guest-right at the well

CUL-06.name: Tamari
CUL-06.customs: dress: linen and kohl; faith: old river gods beside the church; ways: flood-year farming, scribes, canals

CUL-07.name: Sabrans
CUL-07.customs: dress: dyed cloth, jewelled sashes; faith: many faiths side by side; ways: merchant houses, pearl diving, counting-houses

CUL-08.name: Zanari
CUL-08.flavour: East/West African-like savanna farmers and gold traders (Swahili/Yoruba/Akan simple)
CUL-08.customs: dress: bright cloth, gold beads; faith: ancestor spirits; ways: drum and dance, gold weighing, savanna farms

CUL-09.name: Abari
CUL-09.customs: dress: hide cloaks, beadwork; faith: ancestor rites; ways: cattle count as wealth, highland herding, long walks

CUL-10.name: Keshi
CUL-10.customs: dress: light cotton, flowers; faith: many temple gods; ways: spice trade, coast festivals, rice and pepper

CUL-11.name: Eastfolk
CUL-11.flavour: Slavic/Baltic-like forest farmers and river traders
CUL-11.customs: dress: embroidered shirts, fur hats; faith: onion-domed church, icons; ways: forest farms, river barges, bread and salt for guests

CUL-12.name: Skyfolk
CUL-12.customs: dress: wool robes, prayer flags; faith: mountain monasteries; ways: thin-air passes, yak herds, high pastures

CUL-13.name: Ranpuri
CUL-13.flavour: Indian/Bengali-like (with Southeast Asian touches) monsoon rice farmers
CUL-13.customs: dress: wrapped cloth and saris; faith: river-bathing rites; ways: monsoon rice, village councils, festivals

CUL-14.name: Amberfolk
CUL-14.flavour: Polynesian/Malay-like island sailors and pearl divers
CUL-14.customs: dress: shell necklaces, bark cloth; faith: sea spirits; ways: outrigger sailing, pearl and amber trade

CUL-15.name: Corsairs
CUL-15.flavour: Mixed Iberian/Greek/English sailors (pirates and smugglers, nickname-heavy)
CUL-15.customs: dress: bright sashes, earrings; faith: lucky charms and a saint of sailors; ways: raiding, smuggling, nicknames, shares in plunder

CUL-16.name: Leaf People
CUL-16.flavour: Nature-word names (simple, forest-hunter feel; invented, not tied to one real people)
CUL-16.customs: dress: green cloaks, leaf-stitched; faith: groves and old trees; ways: hunting, tracking, hidden camps

CUL-17.name: Cloudfolk
CUL-17.customs: dress: wool ponchos and caps; faith: the peaks as gods; ways: terraced fields, llamas, stone paths, rope bridges

CUL-18.name: Marchfolk
CUL-18.flavour: Mixed English/Welsh/Flemish/Frisian-like borderers (frontier settlers and outlaws)
CUL-18.customs: dress: plain leather and wool, mail where needed; faith: wayside shrines; ways: border raids, frontier farms, feuds, oath-sworn outlaws

CUL-19.name: Sylvari
CUL-19.flavour: Soft Tolkien-style woodland elves (simple, short, lyrical)
CUL-19.customs: dress: long green and silver robes; faith: the old wood; ways: song, archery, slow patient craft

CUL-20.name: Grovers of the Coast
CUL-20.customs: dress: blue-green cloaks, shell clasps; faith: tide and moon; ways: sailing, harbour groves

CUL-21.name: Holdfolk
CUL-21.customs: dress: leather aprons, braided beards; faith: the forge-fathers; ways: mines, craft guilds, grudges kept for generations

CUL-22.name: Horde clans
CUL-22.flavour: Gruff short Mongol/Turkic-tinged orc clan names (simple, harsh)
CUL-22.customs: dress: hides, bone and iron; faith: war gods; ways: clan chiefs, strength decides rank, raiding

CUL-23.name: Tusk clans
CUL-23.flavour: Harsh eastern-steppe orc names (a little more Mongol/Korean-sounding than the Horde)
CUL-23.customs: dress: painted tusks, hides; faith: ancestor bones; ways: steppe living, mounted raiding, clan oaths

CUL-24.name: Hall-giants
CUL-24.customs: dress: furs, huge cloaks; faith: storm and thunder gods; ways: great halls, boasts, sagas, feasts
